newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Oman oil output over 900,000 bpd in Sept - MEES.
newsitem.headline: Oman oil output over 900,000 bpd in Sept - MEES.

text.p: Omani crude output passed 900,000 barrels per day (bpd) in September, some 50,000 bpd more than the sultanate's average 1995 production, the Middle East Economic Survey (MEES) reported on Monday.
"MEES understands that the Omani Government is now planning to attain a new overall production target level of one million bpd in the next few years," the Cyprus-based weekly said.
Oman output hit a new high of 902,600 bpd in September.
Main operator Petroleum Development Oman (PDO) pumped 854,000 bpd last month, Occidental 36,000 bpd, Japex 9,000 bpd and Elf Aquitaine 3,600 bpd, MEES said.
PDO is 60 percent owned by the state, 34 percent by the Royal Dutch/Shell Group, four percent by Total SA and two percent by independent Partex.
MEES earlier reported that PDO's plan to produce 850,000 bpd in September had been delayed till the end of this year because of operational setbacks.
Oman's proven oil reserves stand at more than five billion barrels and gas reserves at 16 trillion cubic feet.
